## Description

Certain output variables don't have similar results between the QNMs and the MSEs. Run sensitivity analyses for the following variables in the specific QNMs:


Fishery 1 - all. aggregate results separately for QNMs that did / didn't match the MSE direction. 

Total Catch - all. aggregate results separately for QNMs that did / didn't match the MSE direction. 

Fishery 2 & spawning biomass - Start with 2-C and 5-A, where both were mismatched.

Use boosted regression trees to examine the relative importance of model edges (linkages) in determining the response of a given well-being variable to a HAB simulation in the Status Quo model based on Melbourne-Thomas et al. (2012): https://esapubs.org/archive/mono/M082/019/tree.r

save the perturbations into a list
```{r echo=TRUE}
PertA <-  c(`inshore small mesh effort`=0)
PertB <- c(`inshore small mesh effort`=-1,`offshore small mesh effort`=-1)
PertC <- c(`inshore small mesh effort`=-1)
PertD <- c(`inshore mesh size`=1,`offshore mesh size`=1)
PertE <- c(`inshore small mesh effort`=-1)


Pert.list <- list(PertA,PertB,PertC,PertD,PertE)
names(Pert.list) <- c("A:Status Quo","B:Rmv sm mesh fleet","C:Rmv inshore sm mesh fleet\nEffort redistribution",
                "D:Increase mesh size","E:Rmv inshore sm mesh fleet")


# Some models require perturbations
# OM 3:  There is a negative perturbation on “inshore recruits”
Pert3.list <- lapply(Pert.list,function(x){c(x,c(`inshore recruits`=-1))}) 

# OM 4:  There a positive perturbation on “climate pressure"
Pert4.list <- lapply(Pert.list,function(x){c(x,c(`Climate pressure`=1))}) 

# OM 5: There is a positive perturbation on "growth"
Pert5.list <- lapply(Pert.list,function(x){c(x,c(`Growth`=1))})
```

## Prep: extract simulation data

Use a custom function to produce two matrices from each QPRESS object: (1) the perturbation response (+1/-1/0) of each variable (column) in each simulation iteration (row); and (2) the randomly simulated weight of each edge (column) in each simulation iteration (row). Bind them together.
```{r}
prep_run_times <- c()
```
```{r}
for(i in c(2,3,5)){
  # get the QPRESS output for all OMs in this HCR list
  tmp_hcr_out <- hcr_out_all[[i]]
  tmp_hcr <- names(hcr_out_all)[[i]]
  print(tmp_hcr)
  
  # for each OM's QPRESS output in this list...
  # for(j in seq(2,length(tmp_hcr_out))){
  for(j in 1:5){
    ## create loop objects
    tmp_qpress <- tmp_hcr_out[[j]]            # QPRESS output object for this OM
    tmp_name <- names(tmp_hcr_out)[[j]]  # name of OM
    if(j==1){tmp_qnm=0}else{tmp_qnm=j}   # OM code number - used for naming file
    
    ## need a vector of perturbations for this OM / HCR combo
    if(grepl("3", tmp_name)){ tmp_p <- Pert3.list[[i]]}
    else if(grepl("4", tmp_name)){ tmp_p <- Pert4.list[[i]]}
    else if(grepl("5", tmp_name)){ tmp_p <- Pert5.list[[i]]} else {
      tmp_p <- Pert.list[[i]]
    }
    
    s <- Sys.time()  # start timer
    
    ## generate matrix from QPRESS output
    tmp_mat <- impact.ss(sim=tmp_qpress,perturb=tmp_p,monitor=NA)
    out <- cbind(tmp_mat[[1]],tmp_mat[[2]])
    
    prep_run_times[length(prep_run_times)+1] <- end.timer(s)
    names(prep_run_times)[length(prep_run_times)] <- paste(tmp_hcr, tmp_name, sep="_")
    
    ## save matrix
    saveRDS(out, here('data','qnm_out','sensitivity',paste0('gbmIn_QNM',tmp_qnm,'-HCR',tmp_hcr,'_',sim.date,'.rds')))
    
  }
  
}
```


How long did that take, on average? (~1-2min each)
```{r}
run_times_df <- as.data.frame(prep_run_times) %>%
  rownames_to_column(var='name') %>%
  separate(col=name, into=c('hcr','om'), sep="_") %>%
   mutate(om=case_when(om=='OM O' ~ 'OM 0 Status Quo',
                      om=='OM 3' ~ 'OM 3 Reduced Productivity', .default=om)) %>%
  rename(run_time_min=prep_run_times)
# save
write_csv(run_times_df, here('data','qnm_out','sensitivity','prep_sensitivity_mats_run_times.csv'))
#

mean(run_times_df$run_time); sd(run_times_df$run_time)
```



*If impact.ss returns an ERROR about having uncertain edges,* first check to make sure that all "Group" numbers from the model data frame (first object in the list of the QPRESS system.simulate output, tmp_qpress) are listed as 'required.groups' on line 40 of the impact.ss function code. Then, check to see if any of your edges are listed twice in the model data frame.

```{r eval=FALSE}
sim$edges %>% unite(From,To,col="edge",sep="-") %>% 
  group_by(edge) %>% summarise(n=n()) %>% filter(n>1)

m %>% unite(From,To,col="edge",sep="-") %>% 
  group_by(edge) %>% summarise(n=n()) %>% filter(n>1)
```

### testing

Test these functions on one example -- fishery 1 catch in OM 2 (Thorson effort) for HCR B

read in input matrix for given QNM-HCR pair

check to make sure the variable response *varies* across the 10K stable matrices recorded from QPRESS (aka, the proportion of matrices with +1 or -1 doesn't = 1.0). gbm needs variation in response to work. 


Use a custom function to produce two matrices: (1) the perturbation response (+1/-1/0) of each variable (column) in each simulation iteration (row); and (2) the randomly simulated weight of each edge (column) in each simulation iteration (row). Bind them together.
```{r}
temp2 <- read_csv(here('data','qnm_out','sensitivity','gbmIn_QNM2-HCRB.csv'))
```

Test: Fit classification tree model with the variable *Emotional & mental health* as the response, for the Status Quo. 
```{r}
# find the column that starts reporting on edges, instead of vertices
d1 <- which(str_detect(colnames(temp2),"_"))[1]
d2 <- dim(temp2)[2]

# grab just edge info
d <- cbind(temp2[,"Fishery 1"],temp2[,d1:d2])

# fitting with gbm step
fit3 <- gbm.step(data=d,gbm.x=2:dim(d)[2],gbm.y=1,family="gaussian",tree.complexity=5, learning.rate = 0.01,bag.fraction = 0.5)

saveRDS(fit3,file=here('data','qnm_out','gbm_QNM2-HCRb_Fishery1Catch.rds'))
```

Use 'summary' to compute the relative influence of each variable in the gbm object. Save to list.
```{r}
fit.sq.df <- as.data.frame(summary(fit3), row.names=NULL) %>%
  rename("Link"=var) %>% mutate(Variable="Fishery 1 catch") %>%
  rownames_to_column("Link2") %>% dplyr::select(-Link2)
```


## Fishery 1 catch

Set up for loop. Create list object to save influence dataframes and timer. The 'counter' is used to add list objects in order (because not all HCR/OM combos will have entries in the list)
```{r}
fish1.br.list <- list()
fish1_run_times <- c()
counter = 1
```

This loop will do a sensitivity analysis for the given variable in all QNM perturbations where that variable had variation in response
```{r}
for(i in c("B","c","D","E")){  # HCRs

  for(j in c(0,2,3,4,5)){  # OMs
    
    # if(j %in% c(0,3) & i %in% c("A","D")){sim.date='20240923'} else{sim.date='20240920'}
    
    # read in gbm input matrix 
    tmp_in <- readRDS(here('data','qnm_out','sensitivity',paste0('gbmIn_QNM',j,'-HCR',i,'_',sim.date,'.rds')))
    
    # if variable differs in response across sims, fit with gbm step
    if(length(unique(tmp_in[,"Fishery 1"])) > 1){
      ## find the column that starts reporting on edges, instead of vertices
      d1 <- which(str_detect(colnames(tmp_in),"_"))[1]
      d2 <- dim(tmp_in)[2]
      
      ## grab just edge info
      d <- cbind(tmp_in[,"Fishery 1"],tmp_in[,d1:d2])
      
      ## fitting with gbm step
      s <- Sys.time()  # start timer
      
      fit.gbm <- gbm.step(data=d,gbm.x=2:dim(d)[2],gbm.y=1,family="gaussian",tree.complexity=5, learning.rate = 0.01,bag.fraction = 0.5)
      ## save fit to list
      fish1.br.list[[counter]] <- fit.gbm
      names(fish1.br.list)[[counter]] <- paste0('QNM-',j,'-HCR-',i)
      
      ## save timer
    fish1_run_times[length(fish1_run_times)+1] <- end.timer(s)
    names(fish1_run_times)[length(fish1_run_times)] <- paste(i, j, sep="_")
      
    ## add to counter
      counter=counter+1
      
    } else{message('skipping QNM ',j,' HCR ',i,' for this variable. no variation in response to perturbation.')}
    
  }
}
beepr::beep()

## save 
saveRDS(fish1.br.list, here('data','qnm_out','sensitivity',paste0('gbmOut_Fishery1_GaussTr5Lr01_',sim.date,'.rds')))
```

## Total catch

Set up for loop. Create list object to save influence dataframes, specify which HCR / OM combos to work through.
```{r}
catch.br.list <- list()
catch_run_times <- c()
```

This loop will do a sensitivity analysis for the given variable in all QNM perturbations where that variable had variation in response
```{r}
counter = 1
for(i in c("A","B","c","D","E")){  # HCRs

  for(j in c(0,2,3,4,5)){  # OMs
    
    # if(j %in% c(0,3) & i %in% c("A","D")){sim.date='20240923'} else{sim.date='20240920'}
    
    # read in gbm input matrix 
    tmp_in <- readRDS(here('data','qnm_out','sensitivity',paste0('gbmIn_QNM',j,'-HCR',i,'_',sim.date,'.rds')))
    
    # if variable differs in response across sims, fit with gbm step
    if(length(unique(tmp_in[,"Total catch"]))> 1){
      message(paste('HCR', i, 'OM', j, sep=' '))
      ## find the column that starts reporting on edges, instead of vertices
      d1 <- which(str_detect(colnames(tmp_in),"_"))[1]
      d2 <- dim(tmp_in)[2]
      
      ## grab just edge info
      d <- cbind(tmp_in[,"Total catch"],tmp_in[,d1:d2])
      
      ## fitting with gbm step
      s <- Sys.time()  # start timer
      
      fit.gbm <- gbm.step(data=d,gbm.x=2:dim(d)[2],gbm.y=1,family="gaussian",tree.complexity=5, learning.rate = 0.01,bag.fraction = 0.5)
      ## save fit to list
      catch.br.list[[counter]] <- fit.gbm
      names(catch.br.list)[[counter]] <- paste0('QNM-',j,'-HCR-',i)
      
      ## save timer
      catch_run_times[length(catch_run_times)+1] <- end.timer(s)
      names(catch_run_times)[length(catch_run_times)] <- paste(i, j, sep="_")
      
      ## add to counter
      counter=counter+1
      
    } else{message('skipping QNM ',j,' HCR ',i,' for this variable. no variation in response to perturbation.')}
    
  }
}

## save 
saveRDS(catch.br.list, here('data','qnm_out','sensitivity',paste0('gbmOut_TotalCatch_GaussTr5Lr01_',sim.date,'.rds')))


## how long did that take?
catch_run_times_df <- as.data.frame(catch_run_times) %>%
  rownames_to_column(var='name') %>%
  separate(col=name, into=c('hcr','om'), sep="_") %>%
   mutate(om=case_when(om=='OM O' ~ 'OM 0 Status Quo',
                      om=='OM 3' ~ 'OM 3 Reduced Productivity', .default=om)) %>%
  rename(run_time=catch_run_times)
# save
write_csv(catch_run_times_df, here('data','qnm_out','sensitivity','catch_gbm_run_times.csv'))
#
```

## Spawning Biomass

Set up for loop. Create list object to save influence dataframes, specify which HCR / OM combos to work through.
```{r}
biomass.br.list <- list()
biomass_run_times <- c()
```

This loop will do a sensitivity analysis for the given variable in all QNM perturbations where that variable had variation in response
```{r}
counter = 1
for(i in c("A","B","c","D","E")){  # HCRs

  for(j in c(0,2,3,4,5)){  # OMs
    
    # if(j %in% c(0,3) & i %in% c("A","D")){sim.date='20240923'} else{sim.date='20240920'}
    
    # read in gbm input matrix 
    tmp_in <- readRDS(here('data','qnm_out','sensitivity',paste0('gbmIn_QNM',j,'-HCR',i,'_',sim.date,'.rds')))
    
    # if variable differs in response across sims, fit with gbm step
    if(length(unique(tmp_in[,"spawning biomass"]))> 1){
      message(paste('HCR', i, 'OM', j, sep=' '))
      ## find the column that starts reporting on edges, instead of vertices
      d1 <- which(str_detect(colnames(tmp_in),"_"))[1]
      d2 <- dim(tmp_in)[2]
      
      ## grab just edge info
      d <- cbind(tmp_in[,"spawning biomass"],tmp_in[,d1:d2])
      
      ## fitting with gbm step
      s <- Sys.time()  # start timer
      
      fit.gbm <- gbm.step(data=d,gbm.x=2:dim(d)[2],gbm.y=1,family="gaussian",tree.complexity=5, learning.rate = 0.01,bag.fraction = 0.5)
      ## save fit to list
      biomass.br.list[[counter]] <- fit.gbm
      names(biomass.br.list)[[counter]] <- paste0('QNM-',j,'-HCR-',i)
      
      ## save timer
      biomass_run_times[length(biomass_run_times)+1] <- end.timer(s)
      names(biomass_run_times)[length(biomass_run_times)] <- paste(i, j, sep="_")
      
      ## add to counter
      counter=counter+1
      
    } else{message('skipping QNM ',j,' HCR ',i,' for this variable. no variation in response to perturbation.')}
    
  }
}

## save 
saveRDS(biomass.br.list, here('data','qnm_out','sensitivity',paste0('gbmOut_SpawningBiomass_GaussTr5Lr01_',sim.date,'.rds')))


## how long did that take?

                      om=='OM 3' ~ 'OM 3 Reduced Productivity', .default=om)) %>%
  rename(run_time=biomass_run_times)
# save
write_csv(biomass_run_times_df, here('data','qnm_out','sensitivity','biomass_gbm_run_times.csv'))
```

## Fishery 2 catch

Set up for loop. Create list object to save influence dataframes and timer. The 'counter' is used to add list objects in order (because not all HCR/OM combos will have entries in the list)
```{r}
fish2.br.list <- list()
fish2_run_times <- c()
counter = 1
```

This loop will do a sensitivity analysis for the given variable in all QNM perturbations where that variable had variation in response
```{r}
for(i in c("B","c","D","E")){  # HCRs

  for(j in c(0,2,3,4,5)){  # OMs
    
    # if(j %in% c(0,3) & i %in% c("A","D")){sim.date='20240923'} else{sim.date='20240920'}
    
    # read in gbm input matrix 
    tmp_in <- readRDS(here('data','qnm_out','sensitivity',paste0('gbmIn_QNM',j,'-HCR',i,'_',sim.date,'.rds')))
    
    # if variable differs in response across sims, fit with gbm step
    if(length(unique(tmp_in[,"Fishery 2"])) > 1){
      ## find the column that starts reporting on edges, instead of vertices
      d1 <- which(str_detect(colnames(tmp_in),"_"))[1]
      d2 <- dim(tmp_in)[2]
      
      ## grab just edge info
      d <- cbind(tmp_in[,"Fishery 2"],tmp_in[,d1:d2])
      
      ## fitting with gbm step
      s <- Sys.time()  # start timer
      
      fit.gbm <- gbm.step(data=d,gbm.x=2:dim(d)[2],gbm.y=1,family="gaussian",tree.complexity=5, learning.rate = 0.01,bag.fraction = 0.5)
      ## save fit to list
      fish2.br.list[[counter]] <- fit.gbm
      names(fish2.br.list)[[counter]] <- paste0('QNM-',j,'-HCR-',i)
      
      ## save timer
    fish2_run_times[length(fish2_run_times)+1] <- end.timer(s)
    names(fish2_run_times)[length(fish2_run_times)] <- paste(i, j, sep="_")
      
    ## add to counter
      counter=counter+1
      
    } else{message('skipping QNM ',j,' HCR ',i,' for this variable. no variation in response to perturbation.')}
    
  }
}
beepr::beep()

## save 
saveRDS(fish2.br.list, here('data','qnm_out','sensitivity',paste0('gbmOut_Fishery2_GaussTr5Lr01_',sim.date,'.rds')))
```

### Distributions: Gamma

I'd like some kind of quantitative comparison...  fit a model to each distribution of relative influence values.
```{r}
library(fitdistrplus)
```

#### By Variable


are the distributions of relative influence values significantly different depending on the variable?
```{r}
m.null <- glm(rel_inf ~ 1, family=Gamma(link='log'),data=fit.df) 
  
m.var <- glm(rel_inf ~ Variable, family=Gamma(link='log'),data=fit.df)

m.var2 <- glm(rel_inf ~ Variable+edge_density, family=Gamma(link='log'),data=fit.df)

m.var3 <- glm(rel_inf ~ Variable*edge_density, family=Gamma(link='log'),data=fit.df)

summary(m.var)
anova(m.null, m.var, m.var2, m.var3, test = "LRT")
```

```{r}
fit.nested <- fit.df %>%
  dplyr::select(Variable,rel_inf) %>%

  nest() %>%
  mutate(my_gamma = map(data, function(x) (fitdist(data=x$rel_inf, distr='gamma', method = "mle")))) %>%
  mutate(shape=map(data, function(x) (x[[1]][1])),
         rate=map(data, function(x) (x[[1]][2])))

fits.gamma <- fit.nested %>% dplyr::select(Variable, shape, rate) %>% unnest(cols=c(shape, rate)) %>%
   mutate(Variable=factor(Variable, levels=c("Total catch", "Fishery 1 catch", "Fishery 2 catch", "Spawning biomass"))) %>%
  arrange(Variable)
fits.gamma
```

## Compare to mismatches

I had a theory that variables with greater spread of relative influence values in a given OM/HCR would be more likely to have a mismatch between the qual / quant models in that particular OM/HCR. I don’t think this is supported by the data.


Read in the data and format as for fig 6
```{r}
speciesALL_compare <- read_csv(here('data','results',paste0('mseVqnm_prob-psim_species1-2_allHCRallOM_',sim.date,'.csv')))

speciesALL_compare %<>% 
  filter(code != "2-A") %>%     # QNM 2 HCR A doesn't have a perturbation
  mutate(variable_out=fct_recode(variable_out,"Fishery 1 catch"="fishery_1_catch",
                                 "Fishery 2 catch"="fishery_2_catch",
                                 "Total catch"="total_catch",
                                 "Spawning biomass"="spawning_biomass"))  %>%
  filter(code != "2-A") %>%
  mutate(equiv=ifelse(abs(psims)<60, 'y','n')) %>%
  mutate(match=ifelse((psims < 0 & prob < 0) | (psims > 0 & prob > 0), "match","mismatch")) %>%
  mutate(match_is_equiv=ifelse(match=='match' & equiv=='y','match, qnm equiv',
                               ifelse(match=='mismatch'& equiv=='y','mismatch, qnm equiv',match))) %>%
  mutate(match_is_equiv=fct_relevel(match_is_equiv, c('match','match, qnm equiv','mismatch','mismatch, qnm equiv'))) %>%
  mutate(model.y=case_when(model.y=="MSE-Species1"~'(sp.1) med longevity',.default='(sp.2) short longevity')) %>%
  separate(code, into=c("OM", "HCR"), sep="-") %>% dplyr::select(-model.x,-psims,-prob,-equiv)
head(speciesALL_compare)
```

### gamma distr
merge data sets.
```{r}
fits_v_match <- fits.gamma2 %>%
  mutate(HCR=ifelse(HCR=="c","C",HCR)) %>%
  left_join(speciesALL_compare, by=c("Variable"="variable_out","OM","HCR"))
```

### specific links

#### all : mismatches
Dive into the most influential links for comparisons where both Species 1 and 2 were off.

First, grab mismatches in both species.
```{r}
compare_mismatch <- speciesALL_compare %>%
  dplyr::select(-match) %>%
  mutate(model.y=ifelse(grepl('sp.1', model.y),'species_1_med_longevity','species_2_short_longevity')) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from=model.y, values_from=match_is_equiv) %>%
  filter((species_1_med_longevity %in% c('mismatch','mismatch, qnm equiv')) & 
           (species_2_short_longevity %in% c('mismatch','mismatch, qnm equiv')))

compare_mismatch %<>% left_join(fit.df, by=c("OM", "HCR", "variable_out"="Variable"))
```


Then check out the top 10% of links for those variables x OMs x HCRs
```{r}
p <- 0.10
fit_by_VOM_mismatches <- compare_mismatch %>%
  group_by(variable_out, Link, OM) %>%
  summarise(mean_ri=mean(rel_inf), sd_ri=sd(rel_inf)) %>%
  group_by(variable_out, OM) %>%
  slice_max(order_by=mean_ri, prop=p) %>%
  unite(variable_out, OM, col="Variable_OM", sep="_") %>%
  mutate(type)

fit_by_VOM_mismatches %>%
  mutate(Link=factor(Link,levels=rev(unique(arrange(fit_by_VOM,Variable_OM)$Link)))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(y=Link,x=Variable_OM, fill=mean_ri)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "YlOrBr", direction=1) +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
  theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45, hjust=0))
```
#### matches : mismatches

Dive into the most influential links for comparisons where both Species 1 and 2 were mismatched VERSUS where either Species 1 or 2 matched. (only one OMxHCR for Total catch had both species 1 and 2 match)

First, grab matches in both species. (we have mismatches from above)
```{r}
compare_match <- speciesALL_compare %>%
  dplyr::select(-match) %>%
  mutate(model.y=ifelse(grepl('sp.1', model.y),'species_1_med_longevity','species_2_short_longevity')) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from=model.y, values_from=match_is_equiv) %>%
  filter((species_1_med_longevity %in% c('match','match, qnm equiv')) | 
           (species_2_short_longevity %in% c('match','match, qnm equiv')))

compare_match %<>% left_join(fit.df, by=c("OM", "HCR", "variable_out"="Variable"))
```

How do the most influential links for this subset compare to the influential links for mismatched variablesxOMxHCRs?
```{r}
v <- 'Fishery 1'
p <- 0.10
# re create the fit_by_VOM but make sure p is the same for both. 
tmp_matches <- compare_match %>%
  group_by(variable_out, Link, OM) %>%
  summarise(mean_ri=mean(rel_inf), sd_ri=sd(rel_inf)) %>%
  group_by(variable_out, OM) %>%
  slice_max(order_by=mean_ri, prop=p) %>%
  unite(variable_out, OM, col="Variable_OM", sep="_") %>%
  mutate(type="matches")
tmp_mismatches <- compare_mismatch %>%
  group_by(variable_out, Link, OM) %>%
  summarise(mean_ri=mean(rel_inf), sd_ri=sd(rel_inf)) %>%
  group_by(variable_out, OM) %>%
  slice_max(order_by=mean_ri, prop=p) %>%
  unite(variable_out, OM, col="Variable_OM", sep="_") %>%
  mutate(type="mismatches")

# plot
tmp_mismatches %>%
  filter(grepl(v, Variable_OM)) %>%
  bind_rows(tmp_matches %>% filter(grepl(v, Variable_OM))) %>%
  mutate(Link=factor(Link,levels=rev(unique(c(arrange(tmp_matches,Variable_OM)$Link,arrange(tmp_mismatches,Variable_OM)$Link))))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(y=Link,x=Variable_OM, fill=mean_ri)) +
  geom_tile() +
  facet_wrap(~type) +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "YlOrBr", direction=1) +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
  theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45, hjust=0))
```
